# smart-protocol — generated capnp bindings for the smart-protocol contract.
#
# One crate at a time, one feature family at a time: `schema-*` compiles exactly
# that family's `.capnp` (plus foundation + transitive imports) via build.rs and
# exposes `schema::<stem>_capnp`. No host mutation, no implementation crate.
#
# The published crate is SELF-SUFFICIENT: it ships the canonical schemas
# (`schema/*.capnp`) and the capnp compiler's own intermediate representation
# (`codegen/<family>.bin`, a serialized `CodeGeneratorRequest`). build.rs feeds
# those requests to `capnpc::codegen::CodeGenerationCommand` — public API, no
# `capnp` binary, no schema tree outside the package — so a crates.io build
# sandbox produces the same bindings a developer gets. The `codegen` feature
# keeps the build-time `capnp` path for development against a working tree.

[package]
name = "smart-protocol"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
description = "Generated Cap'n Proto bindings for the smart-protocol contract: one crate for the whole contract, one Cargo feature per schema family."
license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
readme = "README.md"
repository = "https://github.com/smart-foundation/smart-protocol-rs"
homepage = "https://github.com/smart-foundation/smart-protocol-official"
documentation = "https://docs.rs/smart-protocol"
keywords = ["capnp", "capnproto", "protocol", "schema", "ipc"]
categories = ["encoding", "network-programming", "api-bindings"]
# Published, and publishable: the build needs NO external `capnp` binary and no
# schema tree outside the package (the committed `CodeGeneratorRequest` files
# are the compiler's own intermediate representation). The verification build
# of the packaged `.crate` runs with `capnp` absent from `PATH` and the schema
# tree masked — see docs/PUBLISHING.md for the proof.
publish = true
# Everything the build needs, and nothing it does not: the canonical schemas,
# the committed capnp code-generator requests, the crate root and its build
# script. The development-only script and the publish runbook stay in the
# repository, out of the package.
include = [
    "build.rs",
    "src/**/*.rs",
    "schema/*.capnp",
    "codegen/*.bin",
    "README.md",
    "LICENSE-MIT",
    "LICENSE-APACHE",
]

[workspace]

[lib]
name = "smart_protocol"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[features]
# ─── std ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
std = ["capnp/std", "capnp/alloc"]

# ─── build-time codegen (development only) ──────────────────────
# The published crate never needs a capnp compiler: the bindings are generated
# from the committed capnp `CodeGeneratorRequest` files (`codegen/*.bin`).
# This feature restores the build-time codegen path — the system `capnp`
# binary compiling the schemas — for development against a working tree.
codegen = []

schema-files = []
schema-process = []
schema-settings = []
schema-logging = []
schema-clock = []

schema-audio = []
schema-media = []
schema-power = []

# Shell — desktop session surface: launcher, tray, portals, session control,
#         and the command interpreter.

#

#               history, aliases, variables, environment, jobs, undo,
#               scripts, watchers, bookmarks, guided mode, natural-language
#               interpretation. A REPL asks this.
#
# Merging them would produce one 113-method interface with no single audience,
# which is the shape every schema in this repo has drifted toward.
#
# ── DELEGATION, NOT DUPLICATION ────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The shell ORCHESTRATES; the canonical services OWN their data. Every
# façade below takes and returns the canonical service's types, so there is
# exactly one notification model, one clipboard model, one settings model and
# one app taxonomy in the protocol:
#
#   notifications  ->  notification.capnp  (channels, threads, attestation)
#   clipboard      ->  clipboard.capnp     (history, pinning)
#   settings       ->  settings.capnp      (domain+key, structured values)
#   apps/catalog   ->  appindex.capnp      (one taxonomy, one icon type)
#
# The shell's METHOD SET and ORDINALS are preserved from the official draft:
# every method that existed is still here, at its ordinal, and nothing was
# renumbered. What changed is WHOSE TYPES the façades carry — shell-local

# `ClipboardContentType`, `ShellSettingValue`, `ShellSetting`,
# `ApplicationCategory`) are gone, so there is one model per domain instead of

#

#   shell owns: the tray, portals (file/colour pickers, open-uri), the
#     launcher's own runtime view of an app, session control, and the
#     interpreter surface.
#   notification.capnp owns: notification content, channels, DND.
#   clipboard.capnp owns: clipboard content, history, pins.
#   settings.capnp owns: every setting value.
#   appindex.capnp owns: app catalog metadata, categories, icons.
#   compositor.capnp owns: the session handshake, surfaces, capture.

apps/smart-terminal (thin egui frontend, 3 lines + deep_link)
  → smart-ui-egui (shared components lib, rlib/cdylib: terminal,pty,termlive,shell,appkit,chrome,paint,theme,highlight,icons,overlays,storage…)

        → smart-core (in-process implementation of protocol traits, monomorphized, zero-cost; file ops stay in-process)
```

- `smart-ui-egui` is a **lib**, not a monolith. `apps/files|photos|terminal|eiga` are thin frontends (`src/main.rs 3 lines`, `lib.rs:make_app` + `run_native` + web `start`). - `smart-core` implements protocol traits in-process (VFS, jobs, analysis). No Cap'n Proto socket for `list/copy/search/scan` hot paths. System services (clipboard, process list, AI handshake) go via protocol **doorbell `subscribe → pull(max)/cancel`** (bounded, no flood).
- Old workspace `~/smart/smart-protocol` (94 schemas incl. deleted `filesystem/surface/time`) is archived. Canonical source = `~/smart/smart-protocol-official/schema`. Rust = `~/smart/smart-protocol-rs`.

## 4. Framework-wide hypnotic caret — design system in `smart-ui-egui` (NOT terminal-owned)

> **Ownership rule:** caret lives in `smart-ui-egui` (`theme`/`paint`/`chrome` + `app.rs`/`lib.rs` global visuals), exposed as `caret_*` helpers. Terminal, Files, Photos, Eiga, Settings, AI composer, palette, dialogs all call it. No app forks its own cursor. This section is the contract; §6.2 is only the terminal's inheritance.

### 4.1 What "hypnotic" means (measurable)

- **Breathing**: not a hard square blink. Opacity/width follows a sine `sin(time * 2π * 0.9Hz)`, smoothed through `spring_to(stiffness≈900, damping≈46)` so the caret **glides** to its logical cell instead of teleporting. Write pose: `t = time*2.0; breath = (t.sin() > -0.35) ? 1.0 : pulsing` (`terminal.rs:1717`). Off-peak mid-states are alpha-blended, never popped.
- **Jump**: caret X/Y are spring targets (`term-cx`, `term-cy` in terminal; same `spring_to` calls for every hand-painted field). Typing fast, word-jump (`Ctrl+←/→`), Home/End, line-wrap (`cursor / cols`) — the caret **springs** to the new cell with slight overshoot (`spring_out` family, `w=26,z=0.62`) instead of snapping. macOS-like.
- **Blocked**: block caret shows the char under it in inverted ink (`terminal.rs:1724-1726` — `alpha(#08101e/#ffffff, blink)`), bar caret is 2 px, underline is 2.5 px floor. All three use `cr(2)` — same radius as text.
- **Colour**: `th.accent` (light `#2f6feb`, dark `#6f9bff`) at 0.85 alpha, or gloss `0.62 depending on `cursor_style`. Inactive window: 1 px stroked outline only (`terminal.rs:1729`).

Key structs: `Artifact{mimeType: T.MimeType, data: T.DataHandle}` (any content: text/image/audio/vector/PDF/future), `CapabilityDescriptor{name,parent,inputTypes,outputTypes,parameters: StringMap}`, `ModelDescriptor{capabilities,cost: StringMap,metadata: StringMap}`, `InferenceRequest{request: RequestId, model, inputs: List(Part), output: OutputContract, mode: ExecutionMode{complete|stream|unknown}, parameters: StringMap, budget: Duration}`, `ToolDeclaration/Invocation/Outcome`, `AgentDeclaration/Descriptor/Message/SendResult`, `RetrievalQuery/Hit`, `StreamFrame{artifact,status: more|complete|failed|cancelled,sequence}`, usage metering open-unit (`token|byte|second|joules…`).

### 7.3 Making it real (incremental, reversible, no destructive)

**Phase 0 — contract honesty (no production AI yet).** Panel says what it is: `On-device · rules + search` today. If no backend implements `AI`, UI shows **honest offline mode**: “AI backend not configured — showing on-device tidy + search (local rules)”. Never fake streaming, never invent tokens. Usage chips show `rules/local` not fake tokens.

**Phase 1 — wired handshake/discover (read-only).** On first `Act::Ask`, call `AI.handshake()` (capnp). If succeeds, populate model list in panel header subtitle (`<model name> · <resident>`) and capability chips (from `CapabilityDescriptor`). If fails/timeouts, fall back to Phase-0 rules. This is the **real operational step**: every later action goes through a discovered capability name.

**Phase 2 — `infer` via `InferenceService.derive/stream` (opt-in, reversible).** Send an `Artifact` with `mimeType text/plain` (prompt). Output contract `text/plain` or `application/json` (schema via `DataHandle`). Use `openStream` + `ArtifactStream.pull(maxBytes)` backpressure; show `sequence` gap detection, `StreamStatus` more/complete/failed/cancelled. Handle `unknown` mode: treat as complete. **Tools** declared via `ToolDeclaration` (JSON Schema as `Artifact` `application/schema+json`); invocation via `ToolInvocation`; outcome `union{success, error, unknown}` — never `success=false + nil error`. Agent messages via `AgentService.send` with `AgentSendResult{reply|error|unknown}`.

**Terminal-specific AI actions (all reversible):**

| Action | Input | Output | Reversible how |
|---|---|---|---|
| Explain last error | last block `code≠0`, `cmd`, stderr lines → `Artifact text/plain` | Explanation card (no shell write) | Read-only |
| Fix my command | input line + cwd + error | Proposed corrected line, **fills prompt only** (never auto-runs) | User presses Enter |
| Summarise output | block `lines` (truncated 2500) | Summary card + Copy | Read-only |
| Script this | session history | Draft script block (commented, not saved) | User reviews, then `> file` |
| Clean junk preview | storage `cands` filtered safe | Plan list → Files Cleanup tab pre-selected (already `select_safe`) | Trash confirm still required |

Every write-adjacent action **fills prompt / opens preview / selects**, never `Live::write` without user keypress. `ArtifactStream.cancel` on panel close.

**Phase 3 — knowledge/conversations (later).** `KnowledgeBaseService.query(RetrievalQuery{query: Artifact, topK})` for “find docs about X”. Conversation persistence via `ConversationService.create/append/get(page)`. Store locally; `fork` for branch. **Do not block Terminal on this phase.**

**Backend-agnostic**: terminal never links a model. It holds `AI` reference + `Capability` tokens from handshake. Swapping local ONNX ↔ cloud is backend config; terminal sees same `ModelDescriptor`.

### 10.1 Budgets (gated in CI)

| Metric | Budget | How measured |
|---|---|---|
| Cold start (native) | <800 ms to first painted window | `time` from `SmartApp::new` to first `draw_window` |
| List 1k / 10k | <120 ms / <400 ms, 60 fps scroll | bench `list_dir + sort_entries` |
| Search cached / cold | <50 ms / <3 s first hits | `palette.hits` + `search` path |
| Thumb <16 ms, video first frame <120 ms (cached 8 ms) | display only | Files thumb LRU |
| Copy >85% BW, cancel <500 ms atomic | Job state + file lock | `be.cancel_job` + `JobKind` |
| PTY spawn → first byte | <250 ms | `Live::spawn` bench |
| Live render 80×24 full SGR redraw | <8 ms/frame (16 KiB chunk) | bench `termlive` cell walk |
| Smart render 500 blocks visible | <8 ms/frame (culling) | `draw_terminal` viewport bench |
| Live scrollback 5000×240 cells | <200 MB parser heap cap | `vt100` scrollback 5000 (audit §12 L-10) |
| RSS gate | <350 MB sustained, <600 MB peak (never leak) | `heaptrack`/RSS sampler in test T-PERF |
| Storage scan 50k files | <2 s background, UI thread blocked <8 ms/slice | `storage_pump` step timing |

### 10.2 No-leak rules

- **Textures**: `Icons::cache` `HashMap<(&str,u8,u16),TextureHandle>` unbounded — add LRU 512 entries, keyed by (name,variant,px). Thumbs LRU 512 MiB (`~/.cache/smart-files/thumbs/<fnv>.png`, mtime-keyed), `thumbs.rs` only `video_thumb()` (ffmpeg `scale=min(384,iw):-2`, 2-thread LIFO, cancellable).
- **vt100**: `Parser(rows,cols,5000)` per session; on `close_idx/close_others` parser dropped (child killed, threads joined). `answer` second writer documented (no double-reader). Reader thread exits on `Ok(0)|Err` → `alive=false`, `request_repaint`.
- **Jobs**: `be.cancel_job` atomic — partial copy rolled back or left resumable (never half-file). Storage thread exits on state drop. Graph `force vec![Vec2; n]` allocated per physics tick — cap 190 nodes, reuse buffer (optional micro-opt).
- **History** 500 max (dedup tail 12 shown in palette). **Search palette hits** truncated 8.
- **Audit 600MB**: real cause was texture/scan unbounded growth (`CANONICAL-SPECS.md §5.5`). Fix is LRU on every cache (400 highlight, 8 galley, 500 thumbs, 200 files, 300 tree) + incremental scan. This spec adds: `Icons` LRU, highlight LRU, vt100 cap, Jobs cap.

### 10.3 Multi-thread (no UI block)

- `pty-reader` (1 per Live session). `storage-scan` (1). Thumb workers 2 (Files). Terminal `dir_size/walk/find/grep` are synchronous on UI thread with **budgets**: `walk limit 5000`, `dir_size budget 20_000`, `grep ≤200 files ≤2 MiB ≤200 rows`, `tree ≤300 rows`. Budgets are visible (`… truncated`).
- Never `std::fs::read` whole drive on UI thread; `Scan::step(6)` only.

### 10.4 Process lifecycle (protocol-mapped §11)

- `spawn → wait(timeout) → subscribeDeath → kill` sequence. `top` uses `Process.listProcesses/getProcess` (real CPU/mem), not sine animation (see §12 L-02). `exit` closes session; last session close keeps window (toast). `Live::kill` on drop is SIGKILL — graceful would be SIGTERM→SIGKILL ladder via `signal.capnp` (backend).

### 10.5 Cancel atomic

- Every `JobKind::{Trash,Move,Copy,Compress,Extract}` goes through `be.submit_job` + `draw_jobs_card` cancel (`×` → `be.cancel_job(id)`). Cancel before first byte = no-op; after = current file finishes then stops; state `JobState::Running` → removed. Storage clean = single `Trash` job batch (atomic per item, undo via trash restore). Terminal `live_clear` (`0x0c`) is non-job (screen clear only).
